title: B2+ · L35 — Active listening language
description: Demostrar escucha profunda: mirroring, paraphrasing, verificacion. Habilidad clave de coaches, therapists, leaders.

questions.prompt: Estudias tecnicas de coaching de Chris Voss (ex-FBI negotiator) en su libro Never Split the Difference.
questions.question: 'Mirroring' in active listening means:
options: Mimicking body language and posture only.
Repeating back the last few words to invite elaboration.
Complete silence to let the other speak.
questions.explanation: Mirroring = repetir las ultimas 2-3 palabras del interlocutor con entonacion ascendente. Invita a expandir sin interrumpir ni cambiar de tema. Tecnica central de Chris Voss (FBI hostage negotiator) y de coaching moderno. Registro: coaching, therapy, negotiation, senior management. Formula: interlocutor termina + tu repites las 2-3 ultimas palabras con curiosidad. Error hispano: interpretar como imitacion condescendiente — es lo contrario: signal de atencion maxima.
examples: '...and then it just felt overwhelming.' 'Overwhelming?' → invita a profundizar
'...he completely blindsided me.' 'Blindsided?' → mirroring emocional

questions.prompt: En una sesion de coaching quieres verificar que has captado lo que dijo tu cliente sin usar sus palabras exactas.
questions.question: Paraphrasing shows you understood by:
options: Rewording the content in your own words.
Ignoring and asking a new question.
questions.explanation: Paraphrase = decir con TUS palabras lo que entendiste. Formula clasica: 'So what I'm hearing is X — is that right?'. Verifica comprension y demuestra atencion profunda superior a mero mirroring. Diferencia con mirroring: mirroring usa las palabras del otro; paraphrasing usa las tuyas. Registro: coaching, therapy, executive listening. Error hispano: paraphrasing puede sentirse arriesgado (que si te equivocas?) — pero el otro te corrige y CLARIFICA, resultado siempre positivo.
examples: So it sounds like the real issue is trust, not the deadline itself. Am I close? → paraphrasing con reencuadre
What I'm hearing is you feel unsupported by leadership — is that fair? → paraphrasing con verificacion

questions.statement: 'Uh-huh', 'right', and 'I see' are 'minimal encouragers' that signal you're listening actively.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Minimal encouragers = pequenos verbal cues que dicen 'te sigo, continua'. Sin ellos, el hablante nativo siente que no lo escuchan — silencio absoluto en el otro extremo del telefono se percibe como corte de linea. Fundamentales en active listening y en llamadas telefonicas. Registro: universal en habla anglo. Familia: 'uh-huh', 'yeah', 'right', 'I see', 'mm-hm', 'okay'. Error hispano cultural: algunas culturas hispanas escuchan en silencio total como signal de respeto — en anglo se percibe como desinteres o desconexion.
examples: Uh-huh... yeah... right... I see... → cadena de minimal encouragers en llamada
Just verbal breadcrumbs to show engagement and that the line is still connected. → funcion practica

questions.prompt: En una conversacion dificil con tu manager quieres demostrar escucha profunda de nivel master.
questions.question: Which is the most powerful active listening response?
options: So you're saying X because of Y — does that capture it?
questions.explanation: Paraphrase + causal link + verification = active listening master level. Muestra comprehension profunda (entiendes no solo QUE dice sino POR QUE), no solo atencion pasiva. Formula: 'So you're saying [contenido reformulado] because of [razon subyacente] — does that capture it?'. Registro: coaching, executive listening, therapy. Diferencia con paraphrasing simple: anade el causal link, que muestra comprension estructural del argumento del otro. Error hispano: temer sonar presumptuous — el nativo aprecia la profundidad.
examples: So the frustration is really about being excluded, not the decision itself? → paraphrase con reencuadre emocional
You're saying you feel like you've been set up to fail — did I catch that right? → escucha empatica avanzada

questions.text: It sounds like this has been weighing on you for a while — do I have that right?
questions.explanation: Formula pura de active listening. Fenomeno de connected speech: 'sounds like' con /dz/ cluster asimilado /saʊndzlaɪk/; 'weighing on you' con enlazado /weɪɪŋɒnjuː/; 'have that right' con /vð/ cluster, la /v/ se debilita. Estructura magistral: nombrar emocion ('weighing on'), marco temporal ('for a while'), verificar comprensia ('right?'). Empatia + curiosidad. Registro: coaching, therapy, conversacion emocional profunda. Modelo tipico de escucha terapeutica sin ser therapist.
examples: Sounds like this has been building up for a while — is that fair? → verificacion empatica
I'm getting the sense you've been holding this in — am I close? → hedge suave

questions.prompt: Tu cliente en coaching acaba de mencionar algo intrigante casualmente. Quieres invitarlo a expandir.
questions.question: 'Tell me more about that' is powerful because:
options: It signals genuine interest and invites deeper sharing.
questions.explanation: 'Tell me more' = pregunta abierta magica del coaching. Comunica: 'lo que dijiste me interesa realmente, sigue'. Genera 3x mas informacion que preguntas cerradas (si/no). Registro: coaching, therapy, interviewing (journalism, hiring). Variantes: 'say more about that', 'walk me through that', 'what else?', 'and then what?'. Error hispano cultural: preferir preguntas mas especificas por temor a parecer vago — 'tell me more' es especificamente potente por su apertura.
examples: That's interesting — tell me more about how that felt in the moment. → invitacion emocional
Say more about that. I'm curious where that came from. → curiosidad genuina

questions.prompt: Empareja cada herramienta de active listening con su descripcion:
questions.explanation: Cinco herramientas nucleares del active listening moderno. 'Labeling emotions' viene de Chris Voss (Never Split the Difference) — 'sounds like you're frustrated' / 'seems like you're feeling betrayed'. Nombrar la emocion la desactiva parcialmente (fenomeno neurologico documentado: dar nombre reduce activacion amigdalina). Todos ubicuos en coaching profesional, therapy, hostage negotiation, y executive listening. Registro: coaching y interpersonal deep.
examples: Labeling: 'It sounds like you're feeling betrayed.' → nombrar emocion profunda
Open: 'What was going through your mind when that happened?' → pregunta abierta poderosa

questions.target: It sounds like you're carrying a lot right now — I don't want to rush you. Take your time.
questions.explanation: Master active listening en tres movimientos: emotion label ('carrying a lot') + slow down ('don't want to rush') + permission ('take your time'). Presencia total. Ritmo natural: tempo lento, tono grave y calmado, pausas naturales entre las tres partes. Contracciones: 'you're', 'I don't' obligatorias. Registro: therapy, coaching, conversacion emocional profunda con amigo/familiar. Modelo tipico de intervencion empatica cuando alguien esta al limite. Poderosisimo cuando se entrega con presencia real, no como formula.
examples: Sounds like there's a lot going on. I'm here — take your time. → presencia + permission
I can hear how heavy this is. What do you need right now? → validation + open question

questions.prompt: Analizas por que fallamos al escuchar aunque parezcamos atentos.
questions.question: The WORST active listening habit is:
options: Formulating your response while the other is still talking.
Making eye contact with the speaker.
questions.explanation: 'Waiting to reply' en lugar de escuchar = falla UNIVERSAL de listening. El cerebro planea la respuesta y los oidos apagan; el otro percibe que no lo escuchas realmente aunque asientas. Solucion: presencia total, respuesta despues (comfort con pausa post-otro). Registro: todos los contextos. Error hispano cultural: preparar respuesta rapida por ansiedad de mantener conversation flowing — en anglo la pausa post-otro es signal de escucha profunda, no de vacio. Este es el habito mas destructivo del listening.
examples: Weak: nod-nod-nod, thinking about my reply the whole time. → falso listening
Strong: fully absorbing, then thinking, then responding — with a natural pause. → real listening

questions.statement: Silence after someone speaks is a powerful active listening tool — it invites them to share more.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Silencio deliberado 2-3 segundos despues del otro = magic conversational. Suele hacer que el hablante expanda naturalmente o revele algo mas profundo que no habia planeado decir. Non-natives temen silencio (lo llenan reflexivamente); active listeners lo abrazan como herramienta. Registro: coaching, therapy, journalism, negotiation. Regla FBI de Chris Voss: cuenta hasta 4 mentalmente antes de responder. El otro casi siempre continua. Error hispano cultural: rellenar silencios con preguntas rapidas por incomodidad.
examples: Speaker: '...and that's when I knew.' [SILENCE] Speaker: 'Actually, there's more...' → magic tipico
Silence creates space for depth that quick responses never allow. → principio pedagogico

questions.prompt: En una reunion critica quieres resumir lo que dijo el interlocutor para verificar antes de responder.
questions.question: 'Let me play back what I heard' is a phrase used to:
options: Summarize what someone said to confirm accuracy.
questions.explanation: 'Play back' = resumir para verificar. Metafora de replay de video/audio grabado. Frase de coaches, therapists, senior managers, mediators. Demuestra escucha estructurada y respeto por precision. Registro: profesional-senior, coaching, negotiation. Alternativas: 'let me summarize what I heard', 'let me check I've got this right'. Error hispano: interpretar literalmente como reproducir audio; requiere reconocer el uso metaforico. Uso practico: previene malentendidos costosos en decisiones alto stakes.
examples: Let me play back what I'm hearing: X, Y, Z. Have I captured it? → resumen estructurado
Just to play it back — you're saying the issue is bandwidth, not skill. → verificacion de causa

questions.text: What I'm picking up on is a lot of frustration, but underneath that, maybe some fear too?
questions.explanation: Active listening avanzado nivel terapeutico. Fenomeno de connected speech: 'picking up on' con enlazado /pɪkɪŋʌpɒn/; 'underneath that' con /θð/ cluster; 'maybe some' con enlazado /meɪbisʌm/. Estructura master: 'picking up on' (metafora de radar emocional) + labeling emocion superficial ('frustration') + hedge deeper ('maybe some fear'). Explora emocion subyacente sin imponer diagnostico. Registro: coaching profundo, therapy. Frase con potencial transformador cuando se entrega con presencia.
examples: I'm sensing frustration on the surface, but something deeper too — worry, maybe? → radar emocional
There's anger, but I'm also hearing hurt. Am I reading that right? → doble label + verificacion

questions.prompt: Un amigo te confiesa una situacion familiar dificil que esta atravesando.
questions.question: 'That must be really hard' is best used:
questions.explanation: 'Must be hard' = validation empatica pura. Reconoce dificultad sin minimizar, sin dar consejo no pedido, sin comparar con tu experiencia. Alternativa clave a consejos automaticos que dan la mayoria de personas cuando escuchan problemas ajenos. Frase basica de master listener (therapist, coach, mejor amigo). Registro: emocional-empatico. Variantes: 'that sounds really tough', 'I can only imagine how hard that's been', 'that's a lot to carry'. Error hispano cultural: saltar a dar consejos por costumbre — la validation primero es mas poderosa.
examples: Wow. That must be really hard. → validacion basica poderosa
I can only imagine how difficult that's been for you and the kids. → validacion contextualizada

questions.statement: Active listening includes suspending your own judgment while the other person speaks.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Escuchar juzgando = escucha limitada, sesgada, superficial. Suspender juicio + mantener curiosidad genuina = escucha profunda transformadora. Concepto central de Rogerian therapy (Carl Rogers, 'unconditional positive regard') y de coaching moderno. Registro: therapy, coaching, deep interpersonal. Practica: cuando notes que estas evaluando lo que dice el otro, redirige mentalmente a curiosidad — 'que mas hay aqui?'. Error hispano cultural: en algunas culturas hispanas evaluar activamente es signal de respeto/interes — en active listening es lo contrario.
examples: Don't evaluate — just receive. Analysis can come later. → principio nuclear
Curious, not judgmental. That's the shift that changes everything. → mantra de coach

questions.target: Before I share my thoughts, I want to make sure I've really heard you — can I play back what I understood?
questions.explanation: Frase de oro del active listening senior: pospone opinion propia + verifica escucha + pide permiso respectuoso. Muestra respect + rigor + humildad simultaneamente. Ritmo natural: tempo lento, pausa breve tras 'before I share my thoughts,', tono calmado y curioso. Contracciones: 'I've' obligatoria. Registro: coaching, therapy, senior mentorship, difficult conversations. Marca de coach/therapist/senior mentor experimentado. Modelo transformador cuando se usa genuinamente en conflicto.
examples: Before I respond, let me check I've got it right. → pausa reflexiva estructurada
Rather than jump in, let me play back what I heard first. → priorizar comprension
